mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during tightening periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in two months indicates a weakening labor market, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of rising unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate activity, measured by housing starts, over three consecutive months signals increased consumer confidence and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of rising housing starts.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production by more than 1% in two months signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies face increased costs and reduced output.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of declining industrial production.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4% and the CPI is increasing by more than 0.3% per month, the combination signals a high inflation environment with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
regime_hint: high inflation with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of high inflation and tight monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls by more than 100,000 in a month, combined with an increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3%, signals a weakening labor market and economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases > 100,000 and UNRATE rises > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of weakening labor market conditions.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real GDP by more than 2% in a quarter signals strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of strong GDP growth.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP growth is positive but industrial production declines by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals a supply-side constraint that can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as markets react to the unexpected weakness.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 positive growth and INDPRO declines > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of GDP growth coupled with industrial production decline.
